observations: Black power bank with four integrated cables: Lightning, USB-C, Micro-USB, and USB-A.
Original retail packaging is present, showing brand 'Depak' and capacity '30000mAh'.
Model number 'DP-B23S' is printed on the back of the device.
The back of the device lists multiple output ratings including 9V/2A and 12V/1.5A, consistent with fast charging.
The device has a built-in carrying strap.
The packaging is open and the item appears to be out of the box.

claims.evidence: photo 0 box shows 22.5W PD and device back lists high voltage/amperage outputs
photo 0 shows four cables integrated into the rear housing
printed on box and device but actual capacity is not verifiable remotely

risks.risk: Actual capacity is often significantly lower than labeled on generic brand power banks.
risks.proof: A video of a full discharge test using a USB load tester.

risks.risk: Built-in cables are high-failure points and may be broken internally.
risks.proof: Video showing each of the four cables successfully charging a mobile device.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if cables are non-functional

risks.risk: Battery health may be degraded if the unit has undergone many cycles.
risks.proof: Video showing the device charging a phone while displaying its own remaining percentage.

proof_requests: Video showing each of the four built-in cables charging a phone.
Photo of the power bank's display or status lights while it is charging a device.
Video showing the power bank itself being charged to confirm the input ports work.
response.reason: The brand and model are clearly visible on the device and packaging, allowing for identification. It is priced at the worst-case scenario for a used generic power bank regarding capacity and cable reliability.
